questions.question_hindi:

अभिकथन (A): पिग्मेलियन प्रभाव का एक नकारात्मक प्रतिरूप भी होता है, जिसे 'गोलेम प्रभाव' (Golem effect) कहा जाता है, जिसमें शिक्षक की निम्न अपेक्षाओं के परिणामस्वरूप विद्यार्थी का निष्पादन घट जाता है।
कारण (R): जब शिक्षक विद्यार्थियों से कम अपेक्षा रखते हैं, तो वे उन्हें कम चुनौतीपूर्ण शिक्षण सामग्री प्रदान करते हैं और गुणवत्ताहीन प्रतिपुष्टि देते हैं, जिससे विद्यार्थी का संज्ञानात्मक विकास अवरुद्ध हो जाता है।

questions.question_english:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A): The Pygmalion effect has an inverse negative counterpart, known as the Golem effect, wherein low teacher expectations result in diminished student performance.
Reason (R): When educators hold low expectations for students, they tend to provide less rigorous curriculum content, fewer intellectual challenges, and impoverished feedback, which directly impedes cognitive development.
In the context of the statements above, which of the following is correct?
options_english: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation_english: In educational psychology and organizational behavior, the 'Golem Effect' is the psychological mechanism whereby low expectations placed upon an individual lead to poorer performance, functioning as a negative self-fulfilling prophecy (the direct inverse of the Pygmalion Effect). Assertion (A) is correct. Reason (R) accurately explains the pedagogical causal mechanism: educators who believe certain students are inherently unteachable or low-functioning unconsciously restrict the cognitive depth of assignments, avoid asking probing questions, fail to provide corrective actionable feedback, and allocate less instructional time. This systemic under-stimulation stunts the student's cognitive growth, thereby confirming the teacher's original low expectations. Thus, Both A and R are true and R correctly explains A.
questions.explanation_hindi: शिक्षा मनोविज्ञान में 'गोलेम प्रभाव' (Golem Effect) पिग्मेलियन प्रभाव का प्रत्यक्ष विलोम है, जहाँ किसी व्यक्ति या छात्र से निम्न अपेक्षाएं रखने पर उसका वास्तविक प्रदर्शन गिर जाता है (नकारात्मक स्वतः पूर्ण होने वाली भविष्यवाणी)। अतः अभिकथन (A) सत्य है। कारण (R) इसकी सटीक व्याख्या करता है: जब शिक्षक किसी छात्र को सीखने में अक्षम मान लेते हैं, तो वे अनजाने में उस छात्र को सरल व स्तरहीन कार्य देते हैं, गंभीर प्रश्नों से बचाते हैं, और सुधारात्मक मार्गदर्शन प्रदान नहीं करते। इस उपेक्षापूर्ण व्यवहार के कारण छात्र की वास्तविक संज्ञानात्मक प्रगति रुक जाती है और उसका प्रदर्शन गिर जाता है, जिससे शिक्षक की नकारात्मक धारणा सही साबित हो जाती है। अतः A और R दोनों सत्य हैं और R, A की सही व्याख्या है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Low teacher expectations produce the Golem Effect, leading to diminished student achievement. When educators expect poor performance, they provide less rigorous content, fewer learning opportunities, and minimal constructive feedback, which directly stunts students’ cognitive development and confirms the initial low expectations.

questions.question_english: Achievement Motivation (need for achievement or nAch), prominently studied by David McClelland, is best described as:
options_english: The drive to overcome challenges and achieve high standards
The personal desire to establish and maintain friendly, warm social relations with others
The psychological need to exert control and influence over the behavior of other people
The fundamental biological necessity required for immediate physical survival
questions.explanation_english: The correct answer is (a) The drive to overcome challenges and achieve high standards. In David McClelland’s Three Needs Theory (Acquired Needs Theory), he identified three core human motives: need for achievement (nAch), need for affiliation (nAff), and need for power (nPow). Achievement motivation (nAch) is defined as a learned, internal disposition to strive for excellence, overcome difficult challenges, master complex skills, and meet or surpass high standards through personal agency and effort. Option (b) defines affiliation, option (c) defines power, and option (d) describes physiological survival needs.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर (a) है। डेविड मैक्लेलैंड के तीन आवश्यकता सिद्धांत (अर्जित आवश्यकता सिद्धांत) में उन्होंने मानव अभिप्रेरणा के तीन मुख्य प्रकार बताए: उपलब्धि की आवश्यकता (nAch), संबद्धता की आवश्यकता (nAff), और शक्ति/प्रभाव की आवश्यकता (nPow)। 'उपलब्धि अभिप्रेरणा' (nAch) किसी व्यक्ति की वह अंतर्निहित इच्छा या प्रेरणा है जिसके द्वारा वह कठिन चुनौतियों पर विजय पाने, अपने कौशल में महारत हासिल करने और उत्कृष्टता के उच्च आंतरिक मानकों को प्राप्त करने का निरंतर प्रयास करता है। विकल्प (b) संबद्धता की आवश्यकता, विकल्प (c) शक्ति की आवश्यकता, और विकल्प (d) प्राथमिक जैविक आवश्यकता को दर्शाता है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) The drive to overcome challenges and achieve high standards

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: high standards
David McClelland described Achievement Motivation (need for achievement) as a persistent drive to excel, overcome obstacles, accomplish difficult goals, and meet high internal standards of excellence. Individuals with strong achievement motivation seek personal responsibility for problem-solving, choose tasks of intermediate difficulty, and desire concrete performance feedback.

questions.question_english: Which of the following statements best defines the concept of motivation in the context of educational psychology?
options_english: The cognitive ability to process complex information rapidly
The internal psychological process that initiates, guides, and maintains goal-oriented learning behaviours
The physical maturation of neural pathways facilitating long-term memory retention
The administrative structuring of classroom rules and regulations to ensure discipline
questions.explanation_english: In educational psychology, motivation is defined as an internal psychological condition or state that activates, guides, and sustains intentional, goal-directed learning behavior over time. It provides both the drive (activation) and the directional focus necessary for students to engage with academic content, persist when facing intellectual difficulties, and achieve defined learning outcomes. Option A refers to cognitive processing speed or fluid cognitive ability rather than motivation. Option C refers to neurobiological maturation, which provides physiological readiness but does not constitute the motivational drive itself. Option D relates to classroom management and institutional discipline, which are external organizational controls rather than the internal construct of motivation.
questions.explanation_hindi: शिक्षा मनोविज्ञान में, अभिप्रेरणा (Motivation) एक ऐसी आंतरिक मनोवैज्ञानिक प्रक्रिया या दशा है जो लक्ष्य-निर्देशित अधिगम व्यवहारों को सक्रिय (आरंभ), निर्देशित (दिशानिर्देश) और निरंतर संपोषित (बनाए रखना) करती है। यह शिक्षार्थी को बौद्धिक प्रयास शुरू करने, शैक्षणिक चुनौतियों में दृढ़ता बनाए रखने और अधिगम के लक्ष्यों को प्राप्त करने के लिए आंतरिक ऊर्जा और दिशा प्रदान करती है। विकल्प A अभिप्रेरणा के बजाय 'संज्ञानात्मक प्रसंस्करण गति' को दर्शाता है। विकल्प C तंत्रिका-जैविक परिपक्वता (Neurobiological maturation) को संदर्भित करता है, जो शारीरिक तत्परता तो प्रदान करती है परंतु स्वयं अभिप्रेरणा नहीं है। विकल्प D बाह्य कक्षा प्रबंधन और प्रशासनिक नियंत्रण का हिस्सा है, जो कि अभिप्रेरणा के आंतरिक मनोवैज्ञानिक संप्रत्यय से भिन्न है।

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: and maintains goal-oriented learning behaviours Motivation in educational psychology refers to the underlying psychological forces that spark, direct, and sustain intentional learning activities. questions.question_english: A comprehensive, school-wide leadership strategy led by the Principal to optimize classroom psychology, student well-being, and sustained academic motivation should primarily focus on:
options_english: Maximizing the routine use of external tangible rewards and imposing strict punitive sanctions for non-compliance
Fulfilling fundamental psychological needs for autonomy, competence, and relatedness while cultivating a pervasive growth mindset
Enforcing rigid standardization across all instructional delivery methods to eliminate individual teacher autonomy
Rigidly segregating learners based strictly on prior academic achievement to prevent heterogeneous peer interactions
questions.explanation_english: Self-Determination Theory (SDT), developed by Edward Deci and Richard Ryan, is the premier evidence-based framework for understanding human motivation in educational environments. SDT demonstrates that optimal learning, deep conceptual engagement, and psychological thriving occur when the educational environment satisfies three basic psychological needs: (1) Autonomy (experiencing a sense of volition, personal agency, and meaningful choice in learning); (2) Competence (feeling capable, experiencing masterable challenges, and receiving constructive, growth-oriented feedback); (3) Relatedness (experiencing emotional warmth, social belonging, mutual respect, and secure relationships with teachers and peers). When school leadership embeds these three need-supportive principles into classroom culture and aligns them with Carol Dweck’s Growth Mindset (viewing intelligence as expandable through effort), students develop enduring intrinsic motivation and robust resilience. Conversely, external control, rigid standardization, and tracking (Options A, C, and D) undermine intrinsic motivation. Therefore, Option B is correct.
questions.explanation_hindi: एडवर्ड डेसी और रिचर्ड रयान का 'आत्म-निर्धारण सिद्धांत' (सेल्फ-डिटरमिनेशन थ्योरी - SDT) शिक्षा में अभिप्रेरणा का सबसे प्रामाणिक ढाँचा है। इसके अनुसार, छात्रों में स्थायी आंतरिक अभिप्रेरणा, मानसिक स्वास्थ्य और उत्कृष्ट शैक्षणिक प्रदर्शन तभी संभव है जब विद्यालय का परिवेश उनकी तीन बुनियादी मनोवैज्ञानिक आवश्यकताओं को संतुष्ट करे: (1) स्वायत्तता (ऑटोनॉमी): सीखने में व्यक्तिगत चयन, पहल और स्वतंत्रता का अनुभव होना; (2) सक्षमता (कॉम्पिटेंस): चुनौतियों का सफलतापूर्वक सामना करने और कौशल विकास की अनुभूति होना; (3) संबंधता (रिलेटेडनेस): विद्यालय और सहपाठियों के साथ जुड़ाव, सम्मान और अपनेपन का भाव महसूस होना। इसके साथ जब कैरोल ड्वेक की 'विकासशील मानसिकता' (ग्रोथ माइंडसेट) को जोड़ा जाता है, तो छात्र गलतियों से सीखते हैं और सतत प्रयास करते हैं। बाह्य दंड-पुरस्कार, कठोर मानकीकरण या क्षमता-आधारित अलगाव आंतरिक अभिप्रेरणा को नष्ट करते हैं। अतः प्रधानाचार्य की रणनीति को स्वायत्तता, सक्षमता, संबंधता और ग्रोथ माइंडसेट को बढ़ावा देने पर केंद्रित होना चाहिए (विकल्प B)।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) Meeting basic needs for autonomy, competence, relatedness, and growth mindset

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Meeting basic needs for autonomy, competence, relatedness, and growth mindset Fostering optimal classroom psychology requires fulfilling fundamental psychological needs for autonomy, competence, and relatedness while promoting growth mindsets, supporting sustained academic motivation and well-being.

questions.question_english: When using rewards in a classroom, Cognitive Evaluation Theory suggests that a reward will decrease intrinsic motivation if it is perceived as:
options_english: Informational
Unexpected
Social
Controlling
questions.explanation_english: Cognitive Evaluation Theory (Deci & Ryan) posits that external events, including rewards, influence intrinsic motivation through two primary psychological mechanisms: perceived locus of causality (autonomy) and perceived competence. When a reward is perceived as 'controlling,' the student experiences a shift from an internal perceived locus of causality to an external one ('I am doing this only because they are making me or paying me to do it'). This perceived loss of autonomy suppresses internal desire and decreases intrinsic motivation. Conversely, when rewards are perceived as 'informational' (providing constructive feedback about skill mastery without coercion), they enhance perceived competence and maintain or boost intrinsic interest.
questions.explanation_hindi: डेसी और रयान के 'संज्ञानात्मक मूल्यांकन सिद्धांत' (Cognitive Evaluation Theory) के अनुसार, बाह्य पुरस्कारों का प्रभाव इस बात पर निर्भर करता है कि विद्यार्थी उनका प्रत्यक्षीकरण कैसे करते हैं। यदि किसी पुरस्कार को शिक्षार्थी 'नियंत्रक' (Controlling) के रूप में अनुभव करता है, तो उसके कार्य करने का केंद्र बिंदु (Locus of Causality) आंतरिक से बदलकर बाह्य हो जाता है। विद्यार्थी यह महसूस करने लगता है कि उसका व्यवहार शिक्षक या पुरस्कार द्वारा नियंत्रित किया जा रहा है, जिससे उसकी स्वायत्तता की भावना आहत होती है और कार्य के प्रति उसकी आंतरिक रुचि समाप्त हो जाती है। इसके विपरीत, जब पुरस्कार सूचनात्मक (Informational) होते हैं और सक्षमता का संकेत देते हैं, तो वे स्वायत्तता को नुकसान पहुँचाए बिना आंतरिक अभिप्रेरणा को बनाए रखते हैं। अतः विकल्प (D) सही है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) Controlling

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Cognitive Evaluation Theory explains that rewards impact intrinsic motivation based on how they are perceived. If a reward is experienced as controlling, students feel their autonomy is compromised and attribute their behavior to external pressure. This shift from an internal to an external locus of causality diminishes intrinsic interest in the task.

questions.question_english: To build intrinsic motivation, a Principal advises teachers to utilize ‘Problem-Based Learning’ (PBL). How does PBL foster intrinsic motivation?
options_english: By systematically breaking learning down into repetitive rote memorization drills
By strictly adhering to a traditional textbook-driven passive lecture format
By presenting real-world problems that spark curiosity and inquiry
By guaranteeing high academic grades for all participants regardless of effort
questions.explanation_english: Problem-Based Learning (PBL) fosters intrinsic motivation by immersing students in authentic, complex, real-world problems that provoke cognitive dissonance, intellectual curiosity, and natural inquiry. Grounded in constructivist pedagogy, PBL shifts the locus of learning from passive absorption to active investigation. Working collaboratively to solve realistic dilemmas addresses learners' fundamental psychological needs for autonomy (directing their own inquiry) and competence (mastering challenging tasks). In contrast, rote drills (Option A) and passive lectures (Option B) stifle motivation, while guaranteed grades (Option D) constitute an extrinsic manipulation that dilutes intellectual rigor.
questions.explanation_hindi: समस्या-आधारित अधिगम (Problem-Based Learning - PBL) विद्यार्थियों को वास्तविक जीवन की प्रामाणिक और जटिल समस्याओं से रूबरू कराता है, जिससे उनमें स्वाभाविक जिज्ञासा, आलोचनात्मक चिंतन और सक्रिय अन्वेषण (inquiry) की भावना जागृत होती है। यह उपागम रचनावादी शिक्षणशास्त्र (constructivist pedagogy) पर आधारित है, जहाँ विद्यार्थी केवल ज्ञान के निष्क्रिय प्राप्तकर्ता नहीं होते बल्कि समाधान खोजने के लिए स्वायत्त रूप से कार्य करते हैं। इससे उनकी स्वायत्तता (Autonomy) और सक्षमता (Competence) की आवश्यकताओं की पूर्ति होती है, जिससे आंतरिक अभिप्रेरणा सुदृढ़ होती है। इसके विपरीत, रटना (विकल्प A) तथा पारंपरिक व्याख्यान (विकल्प B) अधिगम को नीरस बनाते हैं, जबकि मनमाने अंक देना (विकल्प D) आंतरिक अभिप्रेरणा के सिद्धांतों के विपरीत है। अतः विकल्प (C) सही है।

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Problem-Based Learning builds intrinsic motivation by confronting students with authentic, ill-structured problems that spark intellectual curiosity and natural inquiry. questions.question_english:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A): Teachers should avoid framing classroom activities as high-stakes, hyper-competitive contests if they aim to cultivate intrinsic motivation in all students.
Reason (R): Highly competitive environments often lead students who perceive themselves as less capable to disengage from learning and adopt performance-avoidance goals.
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options_english: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is true but (R) is false
(A) is false but (R) is true
questions.explanation_english:
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and (R) correctly explains (A).
In educational psychology and Self-Determination Theory (Deci & Ryan), intrinsic motivation flourishes when students experience autonomy, competence, and psychological safety. When classrooms are structured around intense, zero-sum competition, success is defined strictly by outperforming peers rather than personal mastery or intellectual curiosity.
1. Impact on Self-Perception: Students who perceive themselves as having lower academic competence quickly realize they cannot win. Consequently, they experience anxiety, fear of negative social evaluation, and diminished self-efficacy.
2. Adoption of Avoidance Goals: To protect their self-worth from public failure, these students disengage and adopt 'performance-avoidance goals' (strategies aimed at avoiding looking foolish or incompetent, such as withholding effort, feigning disinterest, or engaging in disruptive off-task behavior).
3. Pedagogical Implication: By minimizing zero-sum competition and instead fostering cooperative learning structures and mastery-oriented assessments, teachers encourage all learners to focus on incremental growth, self-improvement, and genuine intrinsic enjoyment of learning.
questions.explanation_hindi:
अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं तथा (R), (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
शैक्षिक मनोविज्ञान और आत्म-निर्धारण सिद्धांत (Self-Determination Theory - डेसी एवं रयान) के अनुसार, आंतरिक अभिप्रेरणा तब विकसित होती है जब विद्यार्थियों को स्वायत्तता, सक्षमता और मनोवैज्ञानिक सुरक्षा का अनुभव होता है। जब कक्षा की गतिविधियों को अत्यधिक प्रतिस्पर्धी प्रतियोगिताओं (शून्य-संचयी या 'जीतो-हारो' स्थिति) के रूप में तैयार किया जाता है, तो सफलता केवल सहपाठियों को पछाड़ने पर केंद्रित हो जाती है।
1. आत्म-धारणा पर प्रभाव: जो विद्यार्थी अपनी क्षमता को अपेक्षाकृत कम आंकते हैं, वे तुरंत समझ जाते हैं कि वे जीत नहीं सकते। इसके परिणामस्वरूप उनमें विफलता का भय, चिंता और आत्म-प्रभावकारिता (self-efficacy) में गिरावट आती है।
2. परिहार लक्ष्यों को अपनाना: सहपाठियों और शिक्षक के सामने अक्षम दिखने से बचने तथा अपने आत्म-सम्मान की रक्षा करने के लिए ऐसे छात्र 'प्रदर्शन-परिहार लक्ष्य' (performance-avoidance goals) अपना लेते हैं और पढ़ाई से पूरी तरह विमुख हो जाते हैं।
3. शैक्षणिक उपाय: अत्यधिक प्रतिस्पर्धी माहौल को कम करके और उसके स्थान पर सहयोगी अधिगम (cooperative learning) तथा व्यक्तिगत प्रवीणता (mastery-oriented learning) पर बल देकर शिक्षक सभी विद्यार्थियों में आंतरिक अभिप्रेरणा और आत्मविश्वास का संचार कर सकते हैं।

questions.question_english: According to Bandura, when a student observes a peer being praised for a specific behavior, the observing student’s likelihood of exhibiting that behavior increases. This is known as:
options_english: Direct reinforcement
Classical conditioning
Vicarious reinforcement
Negative punishment
questions.explanation_english: In Albert Bandura's Social Learning and Social Cognitive Theory, observational learning (modeling) is a cornerstone of behavioral acquisition. When an individual observes another person (the model) experience positive consequences or receive rewards for a specific action, the observer forms a cognitive expectation that engaging in similar behavior will yield comparable positive outcomes. This process is termed 'vicarious reinforcement' (उद्भासित या प्रतिनिधिक पुनर्बलन). Unlike direct reinforcement, where the learner personally receives the consequence, vicarious reinforcement operates entirely through social observation and cognitive appraisal. Conversely, observing a peer face negative consequences for misconduct is termed 'vicarious punishment'. Option A is incorrect because the observer does not directly receive the reward. Option B refers to Pavlovian stimulus pairing, and Option D refers to removing a stimulus to decrease behavior. Therefore, Option C is the correct answer.
questions.explanation_hindi: अल्बर्ट बांडुरा के सामाजिक अधिगम सिद्धांत (Social Cognitive Theory) के अनुसार, व्यक्ति केवल अपने प्रत्यक्ष अनुभवों से ही नहीं सीखता, बल्कि दूसरों के व्यवहार और उनके परिणामों का अवलोकन करके भी सीखता है (प्रेक्षणात्मक अधिगम)। जब कोई विद्यार्थी यह देखता है कि उसके किसी सहपाठी को कक्षा में अनुशासन, परिश्रम या अच्छे व्यवहार के लिए शिक्षक द्वारा सराहा जा रहा है, तो उस प्रेक्षक विद्यार्थी में यह संज्ञानात्मक प्रत्याशा बनती है कि यदि वह भी ऐसा करेगा तो उसे भी सम्मान मिलेगा। इसे 'प्रतिनिधिक पुनर्बलन' या 'उद्भासित पुनर्बलन' (Vicarious Reinforcement) कहा जाता है। इसमें पुनर्बलन सीधे विद्यार्थी को न मिलकर किसी अन्य मॉडल के माध्यम से परोक्ष रूप से प्राप्त होता है। अतः विकल्प (C) सही उत्तर है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) Vicarious reinforcement

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Observing a peer praised for a specific behavior provides vicarious reinforcement, leading the observer to expect similar positive rewards and increasing their likelihood of displaying that behavior.

questions.question_english: To help students handle academic stress, a Principal implements ‘Mindfulness’ programs across the school. In this educational and psychological context, “Mindfulness” refers to:
options_english: Memorizing vast amounts of academic information strictly through rote learning
Paying non-judgmental attention to present moment feelings
Attempting to keep the mind completely blank to avoid stressing about exams
Focusing obsessively and continuously on long-term future career ambitions
questions.explanation_english: In contemporary psychology and education (originating notably from Jon Kabat-Zinn's mindfulness-based stress reduction), 'Mindfulness' refers to paying deliberate, non-judgmental attention to present-moment experiences, including thoughts, physical sensations, and emotions. Rather than trying to empty or blank the mind (Option C) or obsessing about past performance or future exam results (Option D), mindfulness encourages learners to observe their ongoing cognitive and emotional states with acceptance and curiosity. In educational settings, mindfulness enhances emotional self-regulation, dampens amygdala stress reactivity, improves cognitive attention, and reduces evaluative anxiety. Therefore, Option (B) accurately defines mindfulness.
questions.explanation_hindi: जॉन कबाट-जिन (Jon Kabat-Zinn) और आधुनिक संज्ञानात्मक मनोविज्ञान के अनुसार, 'माइंडफुलनेस' (सचेतनता या ध्यानस्थ सजगता) का अर्थ है बिना किसी पूर्वाग्रह, आलोचना या पूर्व-निर्णय के वर्तमान क्षण के विचारों, शारीरिक संवेदनों और भावनाओं के प्रति सचेत और जागरूक रहना। माइंडफुलनेस का अर्थ मन को जबरन खाली करना (विचार-शून्य करना) नहीं है, बल्कि मन में उठने वाले विचारों और तनाव को बिना उनसे विचलित हुए स्वीकार करना और देखना है। विद्यालयों में माइंडफुलनेस का अभ्यास विद्यार्थियों को संवेगात्मक स्व-नियमन (emotional self-regulation), तनाव मुक्ति और मानसिक एकाग्रता में सहायता करता है, जिससे परीक्षा की चिंता नियंत्रित होती है। अतः सही उत्तर (B) है।

Assertion (A): Chronic physiological and psychological stress in adolescents can induce enduring structural and functional alterations in the brain, significantly impeding learning and memory.

Neurobiological research demonstrates the profound vulnerability of the developing adolescent brain to chronic stress:
1. The Stress Response: Sustained academic, social, or familial stress hyperactivates the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis, causing continuous flooding of the bloodstream and brain with glucocorticoids, primarily cortisol.
2. Impact on the Hippocampus: The hippocampus is the primary limbic structure responsible for encoding declarative memory and memory consolidation. It possesses an exceptionally high density of glucocorticoid receptors. Prolonged exposure to high levels of cortisol induces dendritic retraction, loss of synaptic spines, suppression of neurogenesis, and apoptosis of hippocampal neurons.
3. Cognitive Impairment: As the hippocampus undergoes these structural and functional impairments, the adolescent's capacity to form new memories, retrieve stored information, and engage in complex learning is compromised. questions.question_english:
Consider the following statements concerning the neurological and cognitive development of ‘Executive Functions’ in adolescents:
I. Executive functions encompass three core cognitive dimensions: working memory, cognitive flexibility (set-shifting), and inhibitory control.
II. Executive function capabilities reach full neurological and behavioral maturation by the completion of primary schooling.
III. Ongoing structural maturation of the prefrontal cortex (including synaptic pruning and myelination) during adolescence facilitates substantial gains in executive functioning.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
options_english: I and II only
I and III only
II and III only
I, II and III
questions.explanation_english: Developmental cognitive neuroscience identifies executive functions as top-down neurocognitive processes that enable goal-directed behavior: Statement I is correct: Miyake et al. (2000) and Adele Diamond establish that the three core, foundational executive functions are inhibitory control (self-regulation, resisting impulses), working memory (holding and manipulating information), and cognitive flexibility (shifting mental sets and adapting to changing rules). Statement II is incorrect: Executive functions do not finish developing in primary school. Long-term longitudinal neuroimaging demonstrates that executive functions develop across a protracted trajectory that continues through adolescence and into early adulthood (typically until age 22–25). Statement III is correct: During adolescence, the prefrontal cortex undergoes extensive structural reorganization, marked by synaptic pruning (eliminating underused neural connections) and axonal myelination (accelerating neural transmission), which significantly elevates abstract reasoning, long-term planning, and emotional regulation. Therefore, only statements I and III are correct (Option B).

questions.question_english: According to Bernard Weiner’s Attribution Theory of Motivation, a student is most likely to experience the distinct moral and achievement emotion of ‘guilt’ following an academic failure when the failure is attributed to a cause that is:
options_english: External, stable, and uncontrollable (e.g., inherent task difficulty or systemic bias)
Internal, unstable, and controllable (e.g., personal lack of adequate effort or preparation)
Internal, stable, and uncontrollable (e.g., inherent lack of innate cognitive aptitude)
External, unstable, and uncontrollable (e.g., unexpected bad luck or chance events)
questions.explanation_english: Bernard Weiner’s Attribution Theory analyzes how individuals explain the causes of their successes and failures along three primary causal dimensions: Locus of causality (internal vs. external), Stability (stable vs. unstable over time), and Controllability (controllable vs. uncontrollable by the person). Weiner demonstrated that different attributional combinations trigger specific emotional and motivational outcomes: When a student attributes failure to an internal, stable, and uncontrollable cause (such as a lack of innate ability/intelligence), they experience shame, humiliation, and learned helplessness. In contrast, when a student attributes failure to an internal, unstable, and controllable cause (such as insufficient effort, poor time allocation, or inadequate strategy use), they experience guilt. Because effort is unstable (can be modified) and controllable (under voluntary personal agency), the emotion of guilt mobilizes constructive corrective action and redoubled effort in future tasks. Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.question_english: Which of the following is a primary characteristic of a “Mastery-Oriented” classroom environment?
options_english: Student grades are posted publicly on the notice board to encourage competition
The overall speed of task completion is prioritized far above deep understanding
Public recognition is exclusively reserved and given to the highest academic achievers
Errors are treated as normal parts of learning
questions.explanation_english: Achievement Goal Theory (articulated by researchers like Carole Ames and Carol Dweck) differentiates between a Performance-Oriented classroom and a Mastery-Oriented classroom. In a performance-oriented climate, emphasis is placed on outperforming peers, normative rankings, public evaluation, and avoiding the appearance of incompetence. In contrast, a Mastery-Oriented (or task-involved) classroom focuses on individual progress, effort, mastery of content, and deep conceptual understanding. In such an environment, mistakes and misconceptions are not stigmatized as signs of low ability; rather, they are normalized and valued as essential diagnostic feedback indicating where learning is taking place. This psychological safety promotes a growth mindset, risk-taking, and resilience. Options A, B, and C are typical markers of performance-competitive climates that undermine intrinsic motivation and induce anxiety for lower-performing students. Therefore, Option D is the definitive characteristic.
questions.explanation_hindi: उपलब्धि लक्ष्य सिद्धांत (Achievement Goal Theory) में कक्षा के वातावरण को दो रूपों में देखा जाता है: 'प्रदर्शन-उन्मुख' (Performance-Oriented) और 'महारत-उन्मुख' (Mastery-Oriented)। प्रदर्शन-उन्मुख कक्षा में दूसरों से आगे निकलने, कक्षा में सर्वोच्च स्थान पाने और गलतियों को छिपाने पर जोर होता है। इसके विपरीत, महारत-उन्मुख कक्षा में व्यक्तिगत प्रगति, आत्म-सुधार, वैचारिक गहराई और सीखने के वास्तविक आनंद पर ध्यान केंद्रित किया जाता है। ऐसी कक्षा का सबसे प्रमुख लक्षण यह है कि यहाँ गलतियों और त्रुटियों को किसी बच्चे की अक्षमता या कमजोरी के रूप में नहीं देखा जाता, बल्कि उन्हें अधिगम प्रक्रिया का एक अत्यंत स्वाभाविक, सामान्य और उपचारात्मक भाग माना जाता है। इससे बच्चों में असफलता का भय समाप्त होता है और वे कठिन कार्यों को सीखने के लिए तत्पर रहते हैं। अतः विकल्प (D) सही उत्तर है।

questions.question_english:
Consider the following statements regarding the psychology of goal-setting and motivation in school contexts:
I. Proximal (short-term) goals provide immediate targets, enhance self-efficacy, and offer frequent evaluative feedback on progress.
II. Distal (long-term) goals are typically sufficient on their own to sustain focus and motivation in young children over extended periods.
III. Setting learning goals that are excessively easy diminishes task engagement, effort expenditure, and intellectual challenge.

questions.explanation_english: In goal-setting theory (Locke & Latham; Bandura): Statement I is correct: Proximal (short-term) goals provide concrete, immediate benchmarks that allow learners to track incremental progress, experience mastery, and maintain motivation. Statement II is incorrect: Distal (long-term) goals (e.g., 'graduating college' or 'scoring top marks at year-end') are too abstract and temporally distant for young children due to developmental constraints in time perception and executive functioning. Without intermediate proximal milestones, distal goals alone fail to sustain motivation. Statement III is correct: Locke and Latham established that goals must be moderately challenging to elicit optimal effort. Setting goals that are too easy induces complacency, minimizes cognitive engagement, and reduces performance. Therefore, statements I and III are correct.
questions.explanation_hindi: लक्ष्य-निर्धारण सिद्धांत (एडविन लॉक, गैरी लैथम तथा अल्बर्ट बंडूरा) के अनुसार: कथन I सही है: 'समीपस्थ' (अल्पकालिक) लक्ष्य विद्यार्थियों को तत्काल दिशा देते हैं, नियमित प्रगति की प्रतिपुष्टि प्रदान करते हैं और आत्म-प्रभावकारिता को बढ़ाते हैं। कथन II गलत है: छोटे बच्चों में समय और दूरगामी योजना की संज्ञानात्मक क्षमता सीमित होती है। उनके लिए केवल 'दूरस्थ' (दीर्घकालिक) लक्ष्य (जैसे साल के अंत में टॉप करना) प्रेरणा बनाए रखने के लिए पर्याप्त नहीं होते; उन्हें दैनिक या साप्ताहिक छोटे लक्ष्यों की आवश्यकता होती है। कथन III सही है: यदि लक्ष्य बहुत आसान हों, तो विद्यार्थी उनमें कोई चुनौती महसूस नहीं करते, जिससे उनका प्रयास, एकाग्रता और अधिगम स्तर घट जाता है (लक्ष्य चुनौतीपूर्ण किंतु साध्य होने चाहिए)। अतः केवल कथन I और III सही हैं (विकल्प B)।

questions.question_english: Which of the following common classroom behavioral issues is most typically motivated by a student’s misdirected desire to gain immediate attention from the teacher or peers?
options_english: Disrupting the classroom lesson with loud noises or jokes
Quietly daydreaming while sitting passively at the back of the classroom
Skipping school entirely without parental permission or justification
Meticulously reorganizing personal school supplies during instructional time
questions.explanation_english: In Rudolf Dreikurs' model of individual psychology and classroom discipline, students misbehave out of mistaken goals to fulfill their fundamental psychological need for social belonging: Attention, Power, Revenge, and Display of Inadequacy. Disrupting classroom instruction by calling out, making loud noises, telling jokes out of turn, or acting as the 'class clown' represents the quintessential manifestation of attention-seeking behavior. Students displaying this pattern operate under the faulty belief that they only hold significance and status in the group when they are the focal point of attention from the teacher and peers. Conversely, quiet daydreaming or organizing stationery reflects withdrawal or avoidance, and truancy is an escape behavior. Therefore, Option (A) is correct.
questions.explanation_hindi: रुडोल्फ ड्रेकर्स (Rudolf Dreikurs) के बाल व्यवहार और कक्षा अनुशासन मॉडल के अनुसार, जब विद्यार्थियों को कक्षा में सकारात्मक जुड़ाव (belongingness) का अनुभव नहीं होता, तो वे चार गलत लक्ष्यों (mistaken goals) के माध्यम से अपनी पहचान बनाने का प्रयास करते हैं: ध्यान पाना (Attention), शक्ति प्रदर्शन (Power), बदला लेना (Revenge), और अपर्याप्तता का प्रदर्शन (Display of Inadequacy)। कक्षा में अचानक तेज आवाजें निकालना, अनुचित समय पर चुटकुले कहना या विदूषक (class clown) जैसा व्यवहार करके शिक्षण में व्यवधान डालना 'ध्यान आकर्षित करने' (attention-seeking) का प्रत्यक्ष और सर्वविदित उदाहरण है। ऐसे विद्यार्थी यह मानते हैं कि वे केवल तभी महत्वपूर्ण हैं जब सब लोग उन्हें देख और सुन रहे हों। इसके विपरीत, चुपचाप दिवास्वप्न देखना पलायन/उदासीनता है और स्कूल से भागना अनुपस्थिति की समस्या है। अतः सही उत्तर (A) है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Disrupting the classroom lesson with loud noises or jokes

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Classroom disruptions, such as making loud noises, telling jokes out of turn, or acting as the class clown, are classic attention-seeking behaviors. According to Rudolf Dreikurs, when students feel a lack of genuine social belonging, they may seek attention through negative actions to gain recognition from peers and teachers.

questions.question_english:
Consider the following pairs matching motivational theories in educational psychology with their foundational concepts:
I. Expectancy-Value Theory (Wigfield & Eccles): Motivation is governed by subjective expectations of success and perceived task value
II. Self-Determination Theory (Deci & Ryan): Human flourishing depends on satisfying needs for Autonomy, Competence, and Relatedness
III. Goal-Setting Theory (Locke & Latham): Setting specific, proximal, and challenging goals produces superior performance compared to vague goals
IV. Drive-Reduction Theory (Hull): Centers primarily on higher-order intrinsic psychological fulfillment and self-actualization
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
options_english: I, II and III only
II, III and IV only
I, II and IV only
I, III and IV only
questions.explanation_english:
The correct answer is Option A (I, II and III only).
- Pair I is correctly matched: Expectancy-Value Theory (Eccles & Wigfield) posits that students' achievement-related choices and performance are predicted by their expectancy of success and the subjective value they attach to the task (attainment value, intrinsic value, utility value, and cost).
- Pair II is correctly matched: Self-Determination Theory (Deci & Ryan) identifies three universal, basic psychological needs required for autonomous motivation: Autonomy, Competence, and Relatedness.
- Pair III is correctly matched: Goal-Setting Theory (Locke & Latham) demonstrates that specific, challenging, and measurable goals result in higher effort and persistence than easy or vague 'do your best' goals.
- Pair IV is incorrectly matched: Drive-Reduction Theory (Clark Hull) is a physiological/behaviorist theory positing that biological deficits (hunger, thirst) disrupt homeostasis and create internal tension states (drives) that organisms are motivated to reduce to restore biological equilibrium. It does not focus on higher-order psychological fulfillment.
questions.explanation_hindi:
सही उत्तर विकल्प A (केवल I, II और III) है।
- युग्म I सही सुमेलित है: प्रत्याशा-मूल्य सिद्धांत (Expectancy-Value Theory) के अनुसार किसी कार्य को करने की अभिप्रेरणा दो बातों पर निर्भर करती है: कार्य में सफल होने की व्यक्तिगत प्रत्याशा (Expectancy) और उस कार्य का विद्यार्थी के लिए महत्व व मूल्य (Value)।
- युग्म II सही सुमेलित है: आत्म-निर्धारण सिद्धांत (Self-Determination Theory) यह प्रतिपादित करता है कि आंतरिक अभिप्रेरणा के लिए तीन मूलभूत मनोवैज्ञानिक आवश्यकताएं अनिवार्य हैं: स्वायत्तता (स्वतंत्रता), सक्षमता (कुशलता), और सम्बद्धता (सामाजिक जुड़ाव)।
- युग्म III सही सुमेलित है: लक्ष्य-निर्धारण सिद्धांत (Goal-Setting Theory) सिद्ध करता है कि स्पष्ट, विशिष्ट और चुनौतीपूर्ण लक्ष्य सामान्य या अस्पष्ट लक्ष्यों ('सर्वश्रेष्ठ प्रयास करो') की तुलना में कहीं बेहतर परिणाम देते हैं।
- युग्म IV गलत सुमेलित है: अंतर्नोद-न्यूनता सिद्धांत (Drive Reduction Theory - क्लार्क हल) जैविक और व्यवहारवादी सिद्धांत है जो शारीरिक आवश्यकताओं (भूख, प्यास) से उत्पन्न तनाव (ड्राइव) को कम करके शारीरिक संतुलन (homeostasis) बनाए रखने पर केंद्रित है, न कि उच्च मनोवैज्ञानिक संतुष्टि पर।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) I, II and III

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Expectancy-Value, Self-Determination, and Goal-Setting theories are correctly linked to their core concepts. Drive Reduction Theory focuses on tension reduction and biological homeostasis, not psychological fulfillment.

questions.question_english: A secondary school teacher implements Elliot Aronson's 'Jigsaw' cooperative learning model. How does this instructional strategy primarily impact classroom social psychology and student dynamics?
options_english: It cultivates positive interdependence, active accountability, and inter-group social cohesion
It escalates individualistic competition and heightens performance anxiety among peers
It marginalizes and isolates low-achieving or introverted students from group processes
It dispenses entirely with the need for structured lesson planning and teacher mediation
questions.explanation_english: Developed by Elliot Aronson in 1971 to reduce racial conflict and foster integration, the 'Jigsaw Classroom' is a cooperative learning technique where an academic task is segmented among students. Each student in a home group is assigned a specialized subtopic, joins an 'expert group' with peers handling the same subtopic to master it, and then returns to their home group to teach their portion. Because every member's contribution is vital for the team's overall success, the jigsaw method creates strong 'positive interdependence' (Johnson & Johnson), promotes empathy, enhances cross-ethnic and social cohesion, and significantly reduces discriminatory attitudes and competitive anxiety.
questions.explanation_hindi: इलियट एरोनसन द्वारा प्रतिपादित 'जिगसॉ' (Jigsaw) सहयोगात्मक शिक्षण मॉडल में किसी पाठ्य सामग्री को विभिन्न उप-विषयों में विभाजित किया जाता है। प्रत्येक समूह का एक सदस्य अपने उप-विषय का विशेषज्ञ बनने हेतु 'विशेषज्ञ समूह' में जाता है और फिर अपने मूल समूह (होम ग्रुप) में लौटकर अन्य साथियों को वह भाग सिखाता है। इस विधि में प्रत्येक छात्र की भागीदारी पूरी टीम की सफलता के लिए अपरिहार्य होती है, जिससे विद्यार्थियों में 'सकारात्मक परस्पर-निर्भरता' (Positive Interdependence) और सामाजिक एकजुटता का विकास होता है। यह प्रतिस्पर्धा और पूर्वाग्रहों को कम करके सहयोगात्मक भावना का निर्माण करती है। अतः विकल्प A सही उत्तर है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) It fosters positive interdependence and social cohesion

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: cohesion The Jigsaw cooperative learning method structures activities so each group member holds unique information necessary for team success. This approach fosters positive interdependence, encourages peer interaction, and reduces competitive anxiety by making individual contribution essential to group success.

questions.question_english:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A): A teacher noticing a student who is consistently socially isolated (a ‘rejectee’ or ‘isolate’ in sociometric terms) should actively intervene to facilitate their social integration.
Reason (R): Social isolation in classrooms is strongly correlated with depression, academic disengagement, and school dropout.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer:
options_english: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation_english: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) provides the direct causal justification for Assertion (A). In sociometry, peer rejection and chronic social isolation represent grave risk factors in childhood and adolescent development. Decades of empirical studies show that rejected or chronically isolated students experience elevated loneliness, internalizing disorders (anxiety and depression), declining scholastic motivation, and heightened risk of truancy and premature school dropout. Because social isolation produces such devastating psychological and academic consequences, it is imperative for teachers to implement proactive interventions—such as structured cooperative grouping, social skills coaching, buddy systems, and inclusive classroom tasks—to foster their social belonging. Therefore, R directly explains why teacher intervention in A is urgently required.
questions.explanation_hindi: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं तथा R, A की सही और तार्किक व्याख्या करता है। समाजमिति (Sociometry) और बाल मनोविज्ञान के अनुसार, सहकर्मियों द्वारा लगातार उपेक्षित या बहिष्कृत (isolate / rejectee) किया जाना विद्यार्थी के मानसिक और शैक्षणिक विकास के लिए अत्यंत घातक होता है। दीर्घकालिक अनुसंधानों से स्पष्ट है कि कक्षा में सामाजिक अलगाव का सीधा संबंध अवसाद, गंभीर अकेलेपन, चिंता, शैक्षणिक अरुचि और विद्यालय छोड़ने (ड्रॉपआउट) की उच्च दर से है। चूंकि सामाजिक अलगाव के परिणाम इतने गंभीर होते हैं, इसलिए शिक्षक का यह अनिवार्य दायित्व बन जाता है कि वह मूकदर्शक बने रहने के बजाय सक्रिय हस्तक्षेप करे—जैसे समावेशी समूह बनाना, सहपाठी मित्र प्रणाली (buddy system) लागू करना और छात्र को सामाजिक कौशल सिखाना। अतः R, A की आवश्यकता को पूर्णतः स्पष्ट करता है। सही उत्तर (A) है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A

Facilitating peer inclusion directly addresses these risks, explaining why timely social interventions are vital for supporting vulnerable students’ well-being.

questions.question_english:
Consider the following strategies for handling a student experiencing a stress-induced panic attack in class:
I. Speaking loudly to snap them out of it
II. Moving them to a quiet, safe space
III. Guiding them through deep breathing exercises
IV. Immediately calling the entire class’s attention to the student’s behavior
Which combination is appropriate?
options_english: I and IV only
II and III only
I, II and III only
II, III and IV only
questions.explanation_english: A stress-induced panic attack involves an acute surge of the sympathetic nervous system (fight-or-flight response), manifesting as hyperventilation, dizziness, and cognitive terror: Strategy I is harmful: Speaking loudly triggers sensory overload, escalating perceived threat and panic. Strategy II is appropriate: Relocating the student to a calm, low-stimulation environment minimizes sensory input and provides psychological safety. Strategy III is appropriate: Guiding slow, rhythmic diaphragmatic breathing activates the parasympathetic nervous system (via the vagus nerve), lowering heart rate and alleviating hyperventilation. Strategy IV is harmful: Drawing public attention causes intense social humiliation and acute evaluative fear, exacerbating the panic attack. Thus, only strategies II and III are psychologically appropriate.
questions.explanation_hindi: तनाव-प्रेरित पैनिक अटैक के दौरान विद्यार्थी का ऑटोनोमिक नर्वस सिस्टम अत्यधिक उत्तेजित हो जाता है, जिससे तीव्र घबराहट, सांस लेने में कठिनाई और भय उत्पन्न होता है: रणनीति I अनुचित है: जोर से बोलना या डांटना संवेदी अधिभार (sensory overload) और भय को बढ़ा देता है। रणनीति II उपयुक्त है: विद्यार्थी को शांत और सुरक्षित स्थान पर ले जाने से बाह्य उत्तेजनाएं कम होती हैं और उसे सुरक्षा का अहसास होता है। रणनीति III उपयुक्त है: गहरी और धीमी सांस लेने का अभ्यास (diaphragmatic breathing) कराने से पैरासिम्पेथेटिक नर्वस सिस्टम सक्रिय होता है, जिससे हृदय गति सामान्य होती है और घबराहट कम होती है। रणनीति IV अनुचित है: पूरी कक्षा का ध्यान आकर्षित करने से विद्यार्थी लज्जित महसूस करता है और पैनिक अटैक और गंभीर हो जाता है। अतः केवल II और III उपयुक्त हैं (विकल्प B)।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) II and III

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Supporting a student through a stress-induced panic attack requires moving them to a quiet space and guiding deep breathing. Loud reprimands and public attention escalate panic and worsen distress.
